scheme_name: Integrated Basin Development & Livelihoods Programme (IBDLP) – Meghalaya
overview: The Integrated Basin Development & Livelihoods Programme (IBDLP) – Meghalaya is a North East Special scheme aimed at holistic development of river basins in Meghalaya through sustainable livelihood generation, natural resource management, and infrastructure development. It focuses on integrating basin planning with community participation to enhance resilience and economic opportunities in rural areas. The programme targets watershed management, agro-forestry, eco-tourism, and skill development to uplift local communities. It is implemented under the Community & Rural Development Department of the Government of Meghalaya.
objectives: Promote sustainable livelihoods through basin-based natural resource management
Enhance community participation in planning and execution of development activities
Develop infrastructure for water conservation, irrigation, and eco-tourism
Support skill development and capacity building for income-generating activities
Conserve biodiversity and restore degraded ecosystems within river basins
Strengthen local institutions for long-term maintenance of assets
Improve market linkages for agricultural and handicraft products
Generate wage employment and reduce rural poverty
eligibility: The scheme is open to rural communities, self-help groups, NGOs, and local institutions operating in the identified river basins of Meghalaya. Beneficiaries must be residents of Meghalaya and engaged in or willing to undertake livelihood activities aligned with basin development goals such as agriculture, horticulture, fisheries, handicrafts, or eco-tourism. Priority is given to marginalized groups including women, youth, and economically weaker sections.
benefits: Financial support for livelihood projects, technical guidance and training in sustainable practices, assistance in forming producer groups and cooperatives, infrastructure development support (e.g., check dams, irrigation channels), market access facilitation, and convergence with other government schemes for holistic development. Non-financial benefits include capacity building, exposure visits, and handholding for project implementation.
financial_support: The programme provides grant-based financial support to eligible beneficiaries for undertaking approved livelihood and natural resource management activities. Funds are disbursed through implementing agencies in a phased manner based on project milestones and utilization certificates. The quantum of support varies according to the nature and scale of the project, with a focus on cost-sharing and community contribution.
application_process: 1. Identify a viable livelihood or basin development project aligned with IBDLP objectives. 2. Form a self-help group or community organization if not already existing. 3. Prepare a detailed project proposal including objectives, budget, timeline, and expected outcomes. 4. Submit the proposal to the concerned Block Development Officer or District Rural Development Agency. 5. Undergo technical and financial appraisal by the reviewing committee. 6. Upon approval, enter into an agreement with the implementing agency. 7. Begin project implementation after receiving the first installment of funds. 8. Submit periodic progress reports and utilization certificates for subsequent fund releases. 9. Complete the project and submit final report for closure and impact assessment.
required_documents: Land use or site details (if applicable)
Resolution from the self-help group or community body
Identity and address proof of applicants
Bank account details of the organization
Letters of support from local authorities or institutions
implementing_agency: Community & Rural Development Department, Government of Meghalaya
caveats: Funds are released subject to satisfactory progress and utilization of previous installments
Projects must not duplicate benefits from other central or state schemes for the same activity
Beneficiaries must contribute a minimum of 10% of project cost in kind or cash
All assets created under the scheme must be maintained by the community for a minimum of 5 years
Misuse of funds may lead to recovery and blacklisting of the implementing entity
